name: Purple slate
lede: Purple slate is a nearly neutral grey with a purple cast, named Lavender Purple in the old nomenclature of Werner, a mineralogist's scheme of the 1700s, where it is matched to dried lavender flowers, a butterfly's wing and a stone.

sections.title: Werner's lavender purple
sections.body:
In Werner's system, as reissued with natural examples by Syme in the early 1800s, Lavender Purple is described as the lavender blue of Werner, a mixture of blue and red with a little brown and grey [1]. The scheme gave each color three examples, one from animals, one from plants and one from minerals [1]. For this color the animal example is the pale patches on the hind wings' undersides of the peacock butterfly [1]. The plant example is dried lavender flowers [1]. The mineral example is porcelain jasper, a silica stone [1].

The scheme was made for naturalists, not for dyers or painters, so the name carries no recipe or pigment history [1]. A neighboring entry, Red Lilac Purple, is described as campanula purple with a good deal of white and a little carmine [1].

sections.title: The fashion name
sections.body: Garfield reports that the British Colour Council named seven fashionable shades based on Perkin's first color, among them sweet lavender, purple lilac and violet [2]. Sweet lavender in that list is a fashion name, and no link to Werner's color is documented [2]. Lavender here is a dusty purple, nearer to [[lavender]] and [[lilac]] than to a vivid [[violet]] [4].

sections.title: The swatch is greyer than the name
sections.body: The screen swatch is a nearly neutral grey with a slight purple cast, filed in our library as Purple slate, and sits close to the dark plumbago greys [4]. A viewer who expects a flower purple will find it drab. The book's own description includes brown and grey, which is closer to this swatch than to a fresh lavender bloom [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
The swatch measures a lightness of 49 and a chroma of only about 7, with a hue angle of 301 degrees [4]. Its contrast ratio against white is 4.6 to 1 [4]. The nearest distinct named colors are Dark Plumbago Grey, about 3 units off, and Dark Heliotrope Grey, about 4 units off [4].

We have no archive count for this swatch. Screen colors are approximate [4].
